text:
maya.k: Quick sync — thinking about consolidating affinity + credential handoff into a minimal surface so adapters just receive a single 'session manifest'. Pros: fewer handoffs, simpler audits. Cons: bigger secret surface and tighter coupling across hosted/dedicated/private. Thoughts?

samir: I like reducing handshake complexity but we need to be explicit about who can decrypt/access KMS refs. private deployments often require customer-managed KMS/HSM — hosted can't touch raw keys.

zach: We could keep the manifest generic and include opaque references (e.g., `creds_ref`) that the runtime resolves based on hosting mode. That way the adapter only gets resolved secrets when running in the right trust boundary.

alisha: +1 to opaque refs. Main tradeoff: latency and failure modes during resolve. If resolve fails, how do we failover to a lower-tier model or a cached credential? Need clear fallback semantics.

maya.k: Agreed. My straw proposal: small manifest surface with fields: tenant_id, affinity_hint, creds_ref (opaque), ttl, resolve_policy (e.g., eager|on-demand), and audit_nonce. Keep actual key material out of the manifest unless the deployment explicitly allows it (private on-prem with explicit consent).

zach: Example manifest snippet to discuss:
```json
{"tenant_id":"t-123","affinity_hint":"zone-a","creds_ref":"kms://enc/tenant/t-123/session/abcd","ttl":300,"resolve_policy":"on-demand","audit_nonce":"r4nd0m"}
```
This keeps the surface tiny and machine-verifiable.

samir: Two operational items: 1) TTL semantics need to line up with eviction/affinity leases so we don't produce stale routing decisions, 2) RBAC: who can request a manifest that resolves to host-managed keys vs customer-managed keys.

alisha: Also consider telemetry IDs in the manifest so adapters emit consistent traces without leaking tenant identity. E.g., include a hashed telemetry_id separate from tenant_id.

maya.k: Good call. We should also define error classes for resolution failures: `RESOLVE_RETRYABLE`, `RESOLVE_PERMANENT`, `RESOLVE_POLICY_MISMATCH` so higher layers can make deterministic decisions (retry, fallback to degraded model, or abort).

zach: For hosted/dedicated/private differences: - Hosted: runtime may resolve and cache keys (subject to host policy) and perform automatic fallbacks to cheaper model variants. - Dedicated: similar to hosted but with restricted KMS access and customer allowlist. - Private: runtime must not resolve host KMS refs; instead adapter receives a local secret path or a short-lived token issued by customer's KMS gateway.

maya.k: That implies we need a small capability vector in the manifest negotiation: `can_resolve_kms`, `can_cache_creds`, `allows_key_material_in_manifest`. Adapters and control plane can negotiate this at handshake.

samir: Exactly — capability negotiation prevents accidental escalation. We should version that vector, e.g., `manifest_v=2` with backward compatible semantics.

infra-bot: deploy-check: `manifest_v` bump flagged. automated tests triggered: handshake-unit, kms-access-matrix, eviction-ttl-alignment.

alisha: One more corner: traffic routing when affinity changes mid-session (eviction/relocation). If adapter relies on `affinity_hint` for colocated KV caches, we need a migration protocol for cache warmup and a grace period before the new adapter takes over. Suggest `grace_seconds` and `migration_marker` in manifest auth flow.

zach: Implementation sketch: - control plane issues manifest (opaque refs) + capability vector - adapter attempts resolve based on `resolve_policy` - on failure, see error class -> if `RESOLVE_RETRYABLE` retry per backoff, if `RESOLVE_PERMANENT` escalate to fallback route. - during migration, control plane issues short-lived migration manifest with `migration_marker` and `grace_seconds` so downstream can keep KV validity.

maya.k: Action items: 1) samir to draft KMS capability matrix and RBAC rules (by EOD Wednesday), 2) zach to write manifest schema PR (v2) + examples, 3) alisha to propose telemetry/hash scheme and migration fields. I'll collect and turn into a follow-up RFC.

samir: I'll include examples for hosted vs private resolution flows and a few failure-mode runbooks.

alisha: I'll add a short eval plan to detect cache staleness during migration.

zach: I'll prototype the on-demand resolve path and a small test harness for `RESOLVE_*` error conditions.

maya.k: Thanks — if anyone has objections to this direction post here, otherwise I'll start drafting the RFC with the minimal manifest surface + capability negotiation model. :thumbsup:

samir: :thumbsup:

infra-bot: CI: handshake-unit passed, kms-access-matrix pending.
